weakness.title: Missing Response to Physical Security Alerts Outside Business Hours
weakness.description: Physical security alerts raised at night, on weekends or on holidays are not followed by a response, because no one is on duty or reachable to act on them.

extended_description.applicability: Facilities where staffing, monitoring or on-call coverage is reduced or absent outside business hours, while alarms, detectors and access control events remain active. Includes unattended sites and monitoring stations that are not staffed continuously.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person acts when few or no people are present, relying on alerts going unanswered until the next working day.

row.details: Alerts are raised but remain unread until staff return, so detection brings no protection.
Information, media and equipment can be viewed or removed over a long period without interruption.
Equipment can be altered or tampered with over a long period without interruption.

row.description: Staff a monitoring station continuously, or contract an external monitoring service, for areas that need protection outside business hours.
Name a reachable on-call person and a deputy for every period without staff, including weekends and holidays.
Forward an alert to the next person or to a security provider when it is not acknowledged within a set time.
Allow on-call staff to verify and act remotely, and state when a responder must travel to the site.
Trigger test alerts at night and on weekends to check that they are received and answered in time.
A responder must not be sent alone to an unattended site where an intruder may be present. Procedures must say when to call the police instead.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.4 Physical security monitoring
